name: Epitalon
used_for: A synthetic four-amino-acid peptide (Ala-Glu-Asp-Gly) developed by a Russian research group as a pineal gland peptide, promoted online as an anti-aging, telomere and sleep or melatonin peptide. The research is mainly cell and animal work, and the few human reports come from a small set of related research groups, often in non-English journals, with limited methods. There is no good independent human evidence of anti-aging effects.

entries.text: Animal study only, not human data: 1.0 microgram per mouse (about 30 to 40 micrograms/kg) was injected under the skin on 5 consecutive days each month from age 3 months until death.
Animal study only, not human data: 0.1 microgram was injected 5 times a week for about 6.5 months.

internet_entries.text: An educational peptide guide website (PeptidesExplorer) says the standard epitalon protocol is 5 to 10 mg per day injected subcutaneously, with 10 mg per day described as the classic approach, given in the evening. The source gives a range and says no officially approved dosing exists.
internet_entries.population: As described by the source, not a study population

internet_entries.text: A medical education and training site (HubMedEd) says a standard epitalon dosage is 5 to 10 mg per day, sometimes divided into morning and evening doses. The page carries third-party supplier banner links, so it is classed as a vendor-affiliated source and not linked.
internet_entries.population: As described by the source, not a study population

administration_guidance.text: A consumer review site (Innerbody Research) says nighttime administration is considered ideal for Epitalon because of its link to melatonin production, given by subcutaneous injection, with leftover peptide stored in a refrigerator.
administration_guidance.label: internet

administration_guidance.text: An educational blog (The Peptide Breakdown, which carries affiliate links) says Epitalon is often taken in the evening to match circadian rhythm, that a mixed vial is kept at 2 to 8 C and best used within 30 days, and that cloudy or discolored solution should be discarded.
administration_guidance.label: internet

administration_guidance.text: An educational guide (PeptideWiki, which carries affiliate supplier links) says Epitalon has no fasting requirement, unlike growth hormone releasing peptides, that evening use 1 to 2 hours before bed is common, that it is used in short repeated courses a few times a year rather than continuously, and that a mixed vial is kept refrigerated and used within about 3 to 4 weeks.
administration_guidance.label: internet

side_effects.text: In female mice, long-term low-dose Epitalon showed no toxic effect (animal study).
side_effects.label: research

side_effects.text: In a lifetime study in mice, Epitalon did not change food consumption, body weight or mean lifespan, and the authors concluded long-term administration was safe in mice (animal study).
side_effects.label: research

side_effects.text: An educational blog (The Peptide Breakdown) says injection-site irritation may occur and that sleep, circadian or alertness responses vary between individuals, while stating that how often adverse effects occur has not been well established.
side_effects.label: internet

internet_claims.claim: A clinic's educational page claims epithalon reactivates telomerase, extends telomeres, delays age-related disease and supports immunity and regeneration, and suggests combining it with other longevity treatments offered through the clinic.

A telehealth company's page says epitalon extends telomeres in human cells and lengthens lifespan in animals, while stating that human data is observational or uncontrolled, comes mostly from one laboratory, and that long-term safety is not established.

Wikipedia's article describes epitalon as promoted as a telomerase activator, notes that the human data come largely from one research group, and carries editorial warnings about reliance on primary sources and fringe theories.

research.summary: Cell-culture study (Bull Exp Biol Med) from the group that developed epitalon, adding it to human fetal fibroblasts that lack telomerase.
research.finding: Epithalon induced telomerase activity and telomere elongation in these cells. Single-group cell data.

research.summary: Independent laboratory study (Biogerontology) of epitalon in breast cancer cell lines and normal epithelial and fibroblast cells. A published erratum exists for this paper.
research.finding: Epitalon lengthened telomeres in normal cells via telomerase and in cancer cells via an alternative lengthening pathway, which raises the question of whether telomere lengthening is desirable in cancer cells. Cell culture only.

research.summary: Lifelong mouse study (Biogerontology) of monthly epitalon injections versus saline in 54 mice per group.
research.finding: Mean lifespan was unchanged, but maximum lifespan was about 12% higher, and leukemia development was reduced. Total tumor incidence did not differ. Mouse data from the originating research network.

research.summary: Mouse study (In Vivo) of epitalon on spontaneous tumors in one-year-old female C3H/He mice, from an Israeli group; a co-author also published with the originating Russian group.
research.finding: Treated mice had fewer malignant tumor-bearers and no metastases were found, with no toxicity noted. Small mouse study.

research.summary: Russian-language report (Adv Gerontol) on pineal peptide preparations, including epitalon, in old monkeys and elderly people; authors include the originating researcher. Abstract gives no sample size or design.
research.finding: The abstract reports that the peptides restored night melatonin in old monkeys and in elderly people with low pineal function. Design details are not given, so it cannot be judged as controlled evidence.

research.summary: Report (Neuro Endocrinol Lett) from the originating group on epitalon in rats with inherited retinal degeneration and in patients with degenerative retinal lesions.
research.finding: The abstract states that 90% of patients had a positive clinical effect. It gives no sample size, control group or outcome definitions, so it is weak evidence.

research.summary: FDA web page on bulk drug substances for compounding that may present significant safety risks (page dated 04/22/2026, fetched 2026-09-30).
research.finding: On the fetched page Epitalon (epithalon) appears in the table of bulk drug substances nominated but later withdrawn, with FDA noting that compounded drugs containing epitalon may pose a risk of immunogenicity for certain routes of administration due to aggregation. The page does not describe an approved product.

research.summary: 12-year randomized clinical study (Korkushko, Khavinson et al., Bull Exp Biol Med) of epithalamine, the pineal gland extract that came before synthetic epitalon, in elderly people with coronary disease and signs of accelerated aging. Khavinson, who developed epitalon, is a co-author. The abstract gives no group sizes, blinding, dose or course length.
research.finding: After 12 years, deaths were 28% lower in the treated group than in controls, cardiovascular deaths were 2-fold lower, and functional age and exercise tolerance improved. This tested the extract, not synthetic epitalon, and has not been independently replicated.

research.summary: Report (Khavinson and Morozov, Neuro Endocrinol Lett) on thymic (Thymalin) and pineal (Epithalamin) extracts in 266 elderly people followed for 6 to 8 years, with treatment given in the first 2 to 3 years. Written by the developers of these products; the abstract does not describe randomization or blinding.
research.finding: The authors report 1.6 to 1.8 times lower mortality with epithalamin than in controls, and fewer respiratory infections. Extract, not synthetic epitalon, from the originating group, so it is weak evidence.

research.summary: Small study (Korkushko, Khavinson et al., Bull Exp Biol Med) of night-time blood melatonin in healthy elderly people before and after a course of epithalamin. The abstract gives no group size and no control group.
research.finding: Night melatonin rose in people whose pineal gland was initially less active and tended to fall in people with normal pineal function. Extract, not synthetic epitalon.

research.summary: Study (Labunets et al., Bull Exp Biol Med) of immune and hormone rhythms in elderly patients with chronic coronary disease followed for 30 months, who received 6 courses of epithalamin by an 'optimal protocol'. The abstract gives no dose, course length or group size.
research.finding: Rhythms of thymic serum factor and hydrocortisone were retained after the 6 courses, and the authors link this to a milder disease course. Extract, not synthetic epitalon.

research.summary: Study (Khavinson, Goncharova, Lapin, Neuro Endocrinol Lett) of epitalon in female rhesus monkeys of different ages, from the originating group.
research.finding: Epitalon raised evening melatonin in old monkeys and normalized their daily cortisol rhythm. Animal data only.

research.summary: Review (Araj et al., Int J Mol Sci, open access) of 25 years of epitalon research, mostly cell and animal studies. It also describes two human reports from the originating group: a retinitis pigmentosa trial and a 20-day sublingual study in 75 women. The original sublingual paper could not be found in PubMed.
research.finding: The review says mechanisms remain uncertain and that information on short and long-term safety is missing. It describes 5 micrograms per eye for 10 days in 162 eye patients (no side effects reported) and 0.5 mg a day under the tongue for 20 days in 75 women.

dose.summary: No approved dose exists. Human reports describe 0.5 mg a day under the tongue for 20 days, or tiny eye injections. Online sources describe 5 to 10 mg a day injected, which is 10 to 20 times higher, and no human study of those doses was found.

items.text: A 2025 review describes a Russian trial in 162 patients with retinitis pigmentosa (an inherited eye disease) in which each patient got 5 micrograms of epitalon per eye, injected behind the eye, for 10 days. The control group had standard care. This is a single-group report with limited methods.
items.label: research

items.text: The same review describes a study in 75 women that gave 0.5 mg a day of epitalon under the tongue for 20 days, with placebo and control groups. The original paper could not be found in PubMed, so the details are second-hand.
items.label: research

cycle_length.summary: No human study tested repeated courses of synthetic epitalon or what happens after stopping. Studies of the older pineal extract (epithalamin) gave repeated courses over years. Online sources describe 10 to 20 days, once to three times a year, while Innerbody describes 1 month on and 3 months off.

items.text: A Russian retinitis pigmentosa trial gave epitalon for 10 consecutive days, as described in a 2025 review. Outcomes beyond the course were not given.

mechanism.summary: How epitalon works in people is not known. In cells it raised telomerase (an enzyme that rebuilds chromosome ends), and in old monkeys it raised evening melatonin. A 2025 review calls the mechanisms uncertain.

items.text: Added to human fetal fibroblast cells that lack telomerase, epitalon induced telomerase activity and telomere lengthening. Single-group cell data.
items.label: research

items.text: An independent lab found epitalon lengthened telomeres in normal cells through telomerase and in breast cancer cells through an alternative pathway. Cell culture only.
items.label: research

items.text: In old rhesus monkeys, epitalon raised evening melatonin and normalized the daily cortisol rhythm. Animal data only.
items.label: research

items.text: A 2025 review says it remains uncertain whether telomerase and melatonin effects are the only mechanisms, and that physico-chemical and safety studies are limited.
items.label: research

best_documented_effect.summary: No good independent human evidence exists for anti-aging effects. The Khavinson group reports a 12-year mortality benefit, but that study tested the older pineal extract (epithalamin), with few methods details, and has not been replicated.

items.text: A 12-year randomized study of epithalamin (the pineal extract, not synthetic epitalon) in elderly coronary patients reported 28% fewer deaths and 2-fold fewer cardiovascular deaths than controls. Khavinson is a co-author, and the abstract gives no group sizes, blinding or dose. Quality is limited by that and by the lack of independent replication.
items.label: research

items.text: A report from the developers on 266 elderly people found 1.6 to 1.8 times lower mortality with epithalamin than in controls. Extract, not synthetic epitalon. Design details are not given.
items.label: research

items.label: research

side_effect_groups.summary: Human reports from the originating group say no side effects, with little detail. No independent safety trial exists.

side_effect_groups.title: Cancer concern
side_effect_groups.summary: A cell study found epitalon lengthened telomeres in breast cancer cells, which raises a theoretical concern. It has not been tested in people.

items.text: An independent lab found epitalon lengthened telomeres in breast cancer cell lines through an alternative lengthening pathway, which raises the question of whether this is desirable in cancer cells. Cell culture only.
items.label: research

items.text: Peptidepedia says telomerase reactivation is a hallmark of most cancers and that people with active or suspected cancer should be cautious.

side_effect_groups.summary: FDA says compounded epitalon may cause immune reactions from clumping of the peptide.

items.text: FDA lists epitalon among bulk drug substances nominated for compounding and later withdrawn, stating compounded drugs containing it may pose a risk of immunogenicity (immune reaction) for certain routes of administration due to aggregation.

side_effect_groups.summary: Online sources describe mild injection-site reactions, drowsiness and headache, without trial frequencies.
